projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained high mobile device count (16-19) over the past three hours confirms a large gathering or extended guests are currently at the home, which is notable for a Tuesday afternoon. Verifying this aligns with your schedule and helps anticipate increased activity around the dogs.

The steady decline in connected mobile devices from 24 to ~17 between 07:45 and 08:46 strongly indicates the family is leaving for school and work, confirming the Tuesday morning departure routine and explaining the lack of camera activity.

The combination of 21–24 connected devices and zero camera motion over four hours suggests either a large stationary gathering (like a sleepover or guests) or a Wi-Fi presence tracking anomaly, so a quick verification is recommended to rule out false location reporting.

The sustained presence of 20–22 mobile devices on a Monday evening, combined with zero camera activity, strongly indicates a planned indoor gathering (likely a kids' sleepover or family get-together) occupying camera-blind zones. This coherent pattern explains the anomalous device count as normal social activity rather than a security or system issue.

The sustained high mobile device count (21–24) combined with zero camera activity suggests a large gathering or multiple guests are present, providing useful context for evening presence tracking without triggering security alerts.

The sustained count of 19-23 'mobile' devices paired with zero camera activity on a Monday afternoon strongly indicates the presence detector is overcounting IoT or background network devices rather than actual occupants. This matters because it could mask real occupancy events or signal a need to adjust your network's presence detection thresholds.

The sustained presence of 19–24 devices combined with zero camera activity on a Monday afternoon strongly indicates the presence tracker is counting stationary smart devices or the house is unoccupied, suggesting a tracking artifact rather than active occupancy.

The persistent count of 22-25 connected devices on a Monday afternoon, combined with zero camera activity and a recent dip to 19 devices, strongly suggests a network glitch or phantom IoT connections rather than actual occupancy. This mismatch indicates the devices are likely not people, as typical morning departure patterns would normally trigger camera motion.

The persistent count of 22-25 connected devices on a Monday morning, combined with no camera or activity signals, strongly suggests the system is counting smart home/IoT devices rather than people. This could skew occupancy-based automations, so consider verifying actual presence or filtering non-mobile gadgets from your network.

The persistent 25–27 device count alongside zero camera motion at 11 PM confirms a network anomaly (likely ghost connections or IoT device cycling) rather than actual occupancy, which could mask real activity or indicate a connectivity issue.
